newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs recommend ending normal ties with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arabs recommend ending normal ties with Israel.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers recommended on Sunday that their countries suspend steps towards normal relations with Israel, ministers said.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara and Palestinian leader Farouk Kaddoumi told reporters that the same resolution also recommended reactivating the Arab boycott of Israel.
The ministers said the resolution was passed unanimously on Sunday evening at the second session of a regular six-monthly meeting at Arab League headquarters.
It was the strongest concerted Arab response yet to the Israeli government's decision to go ahead with a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

The final text was not immediately available but a draft in circulation earlier recommended Arab states stop normalisation, reactivate the boycott, close down Israeli offices and missions and withdraw from multilateral Middle East talks.
The Syrian minister, asked if the boycott was in the text, said: "Yes, yes, clearly... It is clearer and stronger and it has been adopted unanimously."
Shara looked overjoyed. His country has long said that isolating Israel is the best way to deal with the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Kaddoumi, head of the Palestine Liberation Organisation political (foreign affairs) department, said: "They have emphasised their boycott at the first degree." The first-degree boycott, abandoned by same Arab states over the past three years, bans direct commercial dealings with Israeli companies.

But he added that the ministers did not talk about countries which have signed full peace treaties with Israel -- meaning Egypt and Jordan. Israel could interpret breaking relations as a violation of those treaties.
He said that in line with normal procedure the proposals would have to go to Arab heads of state.
"The aim now is (to obtain) a positive response to these resolutions and to ensure that these resolutions have political effects on the intransigent side (Israel)," he added.
One Arab official said earlier that unnamed Arab states had reservations about the resolutions but Kaddoumi said this was not the case. "The resolutions were unanimous," he said.
